---
title: "Results: Diagnostic Candidate Generation"
---

This section details the narrative of our diagnostic design pipeline—from raw sequence input and quality control filtering to biophysical parameter optimization and specificity verification. 

By running three distinct geographical filtering scenarios, we track how the input database constraints shape the physical profiles and off-target safety of the resulting primer/probe sets:

1.  **Indonesia Only (`indo-only`)**: Tailored strictly to local Indonesian surveillance data.
2.  **Southeast Asia Only (`sea-only`)**: Tailored to regional Southeast Asian strains.
3.  **All-Partial Database (`all-partial`)**: Incorporates local focal strains (Indonesia) alongside global contextual background sequences.

---

## 1. Front-End Data Processing & Quality Control (M01 - M03)

The design pipeline begins with raw sequence ingestion and systematic quality screening to ensure that only high-quality, representative genomes are used for design:

```
[50,750 Raw Sequences] (EpiFlu GISAID)
          │
          ▼ (Module 02 Quality Control)
[20,720 Clean Sequences] (Removed N-content > 5.0%, invalid chars, & duplicates)
          │
          ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
          ▼                         ▼                         ▼
    [Indo-Only]                 [SEA-Only]              [All-Partial]
 (645 Focal Seqs)           (2,680 Regional Seqs)    (6,628 Focal + Contextual)
          │                         │                         │
          ▼                         ▼                         ▼
   [MSA & ML Tree]           [MSA & ML Tree]           [MSA & ML Tree]
```

*   **Sequence Ingestion**: A total of **50,750 raw sequences** from the EpiFlu GISAID segment MP database were loaded into the pipeline.
*   **Quality Control (QC)**: Module 02 filtered out 40 sequences due to high ambiguity ($N$-content $> 5\%$) and 7 sequences due to invalid characters. Identical duplicates were dereplicated, removing 29,983 sequences. This resulted in **20,720 unique, high-quality sequences**.
*   **Subsampling & Filtering**: The clean sequences were then split into our three Spatio-Temporal Filter scenarios:
    *   *Indo-Only*: Subsampling extracted **645 sequences** representing local Indonesian diversity.
    *   *SEA-Only*: Subsampling extracted **2,680 sequences** representing regional Southeast Asian diversity.
    *   *All-Partial*: Subsampling extracted **6,628 sequences** using focal-contextual modeling to balance Indonesian and global representation.

---

## 2. Biophysical Search & Coordinate Selection (M07 - M08)

The filtered sequence sets were aligned, annotated with positive selection markers, and passed to **PrimerLab-Genomic** for primer and probe design. The sequence composition of the input databases had a major impact on the selected target coordinates along the 1,027 bp MP segment:

```
[0 bp] ────────────────────────── Influenza A MP (1,027 bp) ────────────────────────── [1,027 bp]
                │                                                     │
                ├─► Indo-Only (187–341 bp)                            ├─► All-Partial (858–1008 bp)
                └─► SEA-Only  (187–352 bp)
```

*   **Regional Conservency (Indo-Only & SEA-Only)**: Both regional designs placed their target coordinates at the forward end of the segment (**187–352 bp**). In local populations, this region is highly conserved, allowing the engine to place primers with minimal degenerate bases.
*   **Global Shifts (All-Partial)**: When global sequences were included, the 5' region exhibited high sequence entropy. To maintain global coverage, PrimerLab-Genomic shifted the design coordinate to the 3' end of the segment (**858–1008 bp**), which represents the most globally conserved block.

## 3. Specificity Verification & BLAST Veto Filtering (M09)

Before in-silico database validation, candidate primer sets were filtered through the **NCBI BLAST+ Specificity Verification Engine** to prevent off-target amplification in the human host (`human_db`) and cross-reactivity with non-target pathogens (`virus_db`):

*   **The 3' End Veto Filter**: The engine analyzed the 3' terminal region of both primers. If a candidate pair matched any off-target template with zero mismatches in the last 8 nucleotides, it was immediately vetoed (**FAIL**).
*   **Veto Actions in Indo-Only**:
    *   Out of 100 generated candidates, **12 sets were vetoed** due to critical 3' end cross-reactivity with human chromosomes (e.g., Candidate 5 and Candidate 18).
    *   The remaining candidate sets (e.g., Candidate 1, 2, 3) passed all checks and were routed to in-silico validation.
*   **Veto Actions in All-Partial**:
    *   Due to the shift in coordinates, **22 candidate sets were vetoed** due to human genomic cross-reactivity, reflecting the higher complexity of designing primers in the 858–1008 bp region.
